physical.notes: Printed switch-matrix drive column 5, return row 1. Switch Locations description "Left Race Start". The ROM names it "L. RACE START" in T.1 SWITCH EDGES while the host holds public 51 at 1, and clears the name at 0. PinMAME's corvGameData inverted-switch mask inverts this address, so public 1 is an open matrix contact; the ROM reads the switch as active at public 1, so its matrix contact rests closed and normally_closed is true. The matrix page shades the cell 'Opto, Typically Closed'. It is the Opto Track Limit P.C.B. A-18821 at the left lane's start; its pin list (3-20) takes column 5 (J207-5) and row 1 (J209-1). Amendment 16-9890 replaces the board with A-19606. The left lane's start (home) opto of the race track (Track Assembly A-19004). The ROM's T.17 RACE TEST shows it as the LEFT START or POS box; with PinMAME's car models answering (mechanism bits 0 and 1) its self test drove each car to the far end, counting the encoder, and back to the start opto, and accepted the model's pairing. The Switch Locations list prints the start optos with part A-19141 (the Track list's Opto Board Assembly, which carries the encoder P.C.B.) and the encoders with A-18821 (the limit P.C.B.), crossed against the Section 3 board pages, and Manual Amendment 16-9890's page for the Opto Track Encoder P.C.B. A-18822 re-wires it to column 7 rows 1 and 2, which are the engine full-stroke optos 71/72 in the matrix, the ROM and the engine board's own page. The ROM's T.1 names and its accepted race self test place the start optos at 51/52 and the encoders at 55/56, so the device and public address are not in doubt; the records follow the matrix and the Section 3 pages.

mechanisms.behavior: An engine-shaped toy (Engine & Ramp Assembly A-19140) that rocks left and right as a ball shaker. The engine block A-19135 carries four coils (AE-25-1000 on coil brackets; its drawing shows four coil positions and the repair bulletin 16-9887 lists ENGINE COILS (4)) against an engine-shake weldment with a magnet (A-19137); a Hall-effect sensor (A-19230) reads its angle and the Engine Full-Stroke Opto P.C.B. A-18951 reports FULL LEFT (71) and FULL RIGHT (72). The CPU runs it as a servo: it writes the commanded angle to extension register 2, which the Motor Driver Master Board A-18532 latches (U1) for the Slave Board A-18533's AD7524 DAC and LM324/TIP102 coil drivers, and three control bits to extension register 3 (U2), published as 51 (both DISABLE lines, the engine power enable), 52 (LED A lines) and 53 (LED B lines). The commanded angle is not an output address: with mechanism handling bit 2 on, PinMAME's engine model takes the register byte as the position, closes 71 below 64 and 72 above 191, and GetMech(2) returns it. The ROM's T.16 ZR1-LT5 TEST self test raised 51, swept the position down until FULL LEFT closed (63), up until FULL RIGHT closed (192) and parked it at 127, toggling 52 and 53 while the engine moved; ENGINE LEFT drove it to 63. Without an engine answering, the self test drops 51 after about 13 s and shows POSITION OFF and FAILED. T.18 ZR-1 ADJUST raises 51 alone and holds the engine centred while a potentiometer on the Hall Offset Adjust board (Amendment 16-9890) is set; the amendment says the coin door must be closed for engine power, and Adjustment A.2 16 DISABLE ZR-1/LT-5 runs the game with the engine locked down.

The ZR-1 LOW REV GATE (2, SM1-28-900-DC, in the engine ramp, which carries a flopgate, a front gate and a back gate), the ZR-1 UP REV GATE (5, SM1-35-4000-DC, which the amendment's back-panel Ball Gate Actuator carries) and the ZR-1 LOCKUP coil (15, AE-30-2000, Eject Assembly A-15368-1) act on the lock. The rules light LT-5 LOCK from the left outer loop; Adjustment A.2 13 ENDGAME LOCK REL. decides whether locked balls are released at game end. No retained source says which gate opens or closes which path or in what order the ROM fires 2, 5 and 15 to lock and release.

The Dual H-Drive Motor Controller A-19159 takes RACE DIRECTION (17) for both cars and LEFT/RIGHT RACE ENABLE (18, 19) for each motor. Each lane has a start (limit) opto, 51 left and 52 right, and an encoder opto on its cord pulley, 55 and 56. The ROM's T.17 RACE TEST self test drove the left car with 17 and 18 on, counting its encoder to 670 while 51 opened, then the right car with 17 and 19 to 638, then returned both to their start optos at count 0; LEFT FORWARD raised 17 and 18 and the left car's count climbed while Enter was held. With PinMAME's car models (mechanism bits 0 and 1), which move a car forward while 17 is on, that is consistent with 17 on meaning forward. During the CORVETTE CHALLENGE the machine's car moves at a steady pace and the player's car advances as shots are made; a six-lamp race tree (81-86) stands over the track.

physical.notes: Custom output 1: corvGameData declares three custom solenoids, and corv_getSol publishes bit 0 of the CPU's extension register 3 here (CORE_CUSTSOLNO(1)). That register is the Motor Driver Master Board A-18532's U2 latch (strobe DIS2 from CPU J204), whose bit-0 output drives both the DISABLE A and DISABLE B lines through the ULN2803 to the Slave Board, the engine coils' driver. The ROM raises it on entering T.16 ZR1-LT5 TEST and keeps it on, raises it alone in T.18 ZR-1 ADJUST, and drops it when the self test fails, so it is the engine power enable.
